contexts.text: (To restore the silver) of each into his sack () = wherever there was a receptacle in the Natural. A sack = a receptacle... A sack, here, in special, = what is scientific; for, as a sack is a receptacle of corn, so is what is scientific a receptacle of good.
A sack = a receptacle in the Natural; and to open it = to observe.
A sack = a receptacle. AC 5531, Explained.
Sacks = receptacles in the Natural, thus the Natural.
(Spirits seen) carrying sacks in which were raw materials. SE 4627:12.
Great purses which appeared like sacks, containing money. Seen and Explained. TCR 277. SE 3605.
Carry the things of religion as it were in a sack on their backs. TCR 146.
On the other side of Gehenna was seen a great sack, out of which when opened there flew a dense and black smoke... which indicates such hatred.
A great [piece] of silver conveyed into the pocket of my garment. Explained.
He was into the veil, as into a sack.
He was wrapped in a cloth... like a pyramidal sack... which was then whirled about. Described.
(These Spirits) sometimes put industrious Spirits into a state of somnolence, which they call putting them into a sack.
